info.name: WABA Connect — Send Money (WhatsApp Flows)
info.description: End-to-end Send Money journey without a phone: seed demo data, start a session, walk every Flow screen, create the order, pay through the mock gateway's signed callback and complete the payout. Run the folders in order. Requires a Development backend with Remittance:Enabled and Remittance:DevTools:Enabled. See docs/remittance/SEND_MONEY_WALKTHROUGH.md.

request.description: Bearer token for the admin endpoints (Setup › Send Money, Transfers).
Idempotent. MYR → IDR, PHP, INR, BDT, SGD, VND with payout methods, recipient fields, banks, fees, regulatory lists, FPX and Pay-at-Counter, and the 'Send Money' bot flow.
Calls the configured exchange-rate provider. ok=false with an error when no fresh rate is available — never an invented one.

item.name: 2. Flow journey (plaintext harness)
item.description: The same handler the encrypted Meta endpoint uses, without encryption.

request.description: What the bot's WhatsApp Flow node does, minus sending the message. Creates the contact if needed.
The mock OTP provider delivers nothing; with Remittance:Otp:Mock:ExposeCodeInFlow the code appears as a development hint.

exec: pm.test('mock OTP exposed in Development', () => pm.expect(m).to.not.be.null);

request.description: Server-side enforcement: every later action requires a verified session.
f1..f6 are the payout method's recipient fields in slot order (see the fields request).
Creates the order (AwaitingPayment / Pending) and starts the payment with the provider. Never marks it paid.
RSA-OAEP-SHA256 wraps a fresh AES-128 key; the payload is AES-GCM with a 16-byte IV — exactly Meta's scheme.

item.name: POST encrypted request to the real endpoint

request.description: The response is encrypted with the bit-flipped IV.
432 instead when a signature is required (Production, or a configured app secret with a wrong header).

exec: pm.test('421 makes WhatsApp refetch the key', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([421, 432]));

request.description: Payment can only change through a provider callback whose signature verifies.
What the checkout page's button does: builds the gateway's callback, signs it and sends it through the same verification as /api/webhook/payments/Mock. The queue worker then applies it.
Then call /api/webhook/payments/Mock with header X-Mock-Signature and the same body; change one character to see 401.
